newsitem.title: GREECE: Athens stocks climb 0.54 pct, hit new year high.
newsitem.headline: Athens stocks climb 0.54 pct, hit new year high.

text.p: Greek stocks hit new year highs on Tuesday with the benchmark index rising 0.54 percent to 1,464.75 on the first trading session following the four-day Orthodox Easter recess.
Market watchers said they were confident that Greek stocks were heading higher in the short- and medium-term.

"The market's upside potential is very good and the 1,500 level, a mere way point to year-end targets above 1,700, should be conquered in the coming few sessions," said George Politis, head of institutional sales with Eurosec Securities.
There were indications of increasing foreign buying activity in the Athens bourse which is expected to become stronger in the coming months, brokers said.
"A lower political risk associated with Greece has given rise to large scope for additional placements in Greek stocks by foreign institutionals," he said.
Banks and industrials appear to be the prime targets for domestic and international institutional postfolios.
"I expect banks and industrial blue chips with good earnings growth potential to continue attracting institutional funds and pulling the market higher," Politis said.
Other sectors, such as leasing, holding and commercials are currently priced very low, but would only attract capital gains from large cap stocks, he said.

The Athens general share index ended 0.54 percent or 7.80 points higher on Tuesday, at 1,464.75, from Thursday's close of 1,456.95. It opened at 1459.85 and reached an intra-day and year high of 1,473.64 points at mid-session.
Banks lifted the index with a 0.93 percent advance.
Industrials and construction followed with 0.32 and 0.35 percent increases.
Turnover was fairly moderate at 12.6 billion drachmas on 4.1 million shares traded.
Advancers beat decliners 139 to 75, with 26 stocks unchanged on 240 traded.
The Merrill Lynch call spread warrant on OTE with a strike price of 3,800 drachmas was quoted higher at 1,085.0 - 1,115.0. Shares of OTE telecom, the underlying, were down 20 drachmas at 6,200.

The ING Baring Financial Products American style call warrant based on a basket of six bank stocks was quoted higher at $63.43-$65.12. The strike price is set at $99.60 and the warrants expire October 8, 1997.
The ING Baring Financial Products American- style call warrant on a basket of six blue-chips denominated in drachmas was quoted lower at 2,296-2,494 drachmas.
The strike price is set at 10,000 drachmas and the warrants expire on February 2, 1998.

The recently launched ING Baring American-style second call warrant on a basket of six bank stocks was quoted higher at $13.88-N/O. The strike price is set at $110.0 and the warrants expire April 9 1998.
